cover.alt: Tansy holds up a bark map as Pebble and Moss set off by the stream

text: It was a cool fall morning in Willowbrook Hollow. The leaves were red and gold.
Tansy the squirrel was digging. She dug by the stream. She dug by the stump. She dug by the gate.
Dirt went up. Dirt went down. Dirt went on Moss.
“Tansy,” said Moss kindly. “You are digging on me.”

media.alt: Tansy digs holes all over the Hollow and gets dirt on Moss

text: “Sorry, Moss!” said Tansy. “I lost my acorns! All one hundred of them!”
Moss shook the dirt off his spines.
“Last fall, I hid them,” said Tansy. “Then I made a map, so I would not forget. Then I forgot what the map means!”
She held up a scrap of bark. On it were lines and dots and one big X.

media.alt: Tansy holds up a bark map while Moss shakes off the dirt

text: Moss looked at the map. He looked for a long time. Moss liked to look at small things.
There was a wavy line. There was a rock that looked like a frog. There was a log with a hole. And at the top, there was an X.
“X is where the acorns are,” said Tansy. “It is treasure! Acorn treasure!”
“It looks like a long walk,” said Moss.

media.alt: Moss looks closely at the map with its wavy line, frog rock, log and X

text: Just then, Pip and Pebble ran by. They were fussing, as they always do.
Pip peeked at the map. “That map is upside down,” he said.
“It is not,” said Pebble. “YOU are upside down.”
“I am not!” said Pip.
“Then stand on your head and check,” said Pebble.
Pip huffed and ran off. Pebble stayed. “I will come on this adventure,” she said. “Just to show Pip who is boss.”

media.alt: Pip and Pebble argue about the map while Tansy and Moss watch

text: Pebble had a bag of scraps. She had string, a bent nail, a cork and a shell.
“What is all that for?” asked Moss.
“I do not know yet,” said Pebble. “That is the fun part.”
Tansy was hopping up and down. “Step one: we go! Step two: we go fast! Step three: we… um… we go!”
“That is the same step three times,” said Pebble.

media.alt: Pebble shows her bag of scraps while Tansy hops

text: Moss did not like long walks. He did not like new spots. He liked his stream and his bush and his snack of bugs.
But Tansy was his best friend. And Tansy was bad at maps.
Moss took a deep breath. “I will come,” he said softly. “Someone has to look at the small things.”
Tansy gave him a hug. It was a spiky hug. She did not mind.

media.alt: Tansy gives Moss a spiky hug

text: The wavy line on the map was the stream. The stream was fast and cold. It went splish and splash on the rocks.
“We have to get across,” said Tansy. “Step one: we jump!”
“YOU can jump,” said Pebble. “You are a squirrel. Moss is a hedgehog. Hedgehogs are bad at jumping.”
Moss nodded. It was true.

media.alt: Tansy, Pebble and Moss stand by the fast stream

text: Pebble dug in her bag. She made a raft of sticks and string. Then she put a big flat leaf on top.
“A raft!” said Tansy.
“A boat,” said Pebble.
“A raft is a boat,” said Tansy.
Pebble frowned. “Do not finish what I say,” she said. “That is Pip’s job. And he does it badly.”

media.alt: Pebble builds a raft from sticks, string and a leaf

text: Moss sat on the raft. Pebble sat on Moss. That was a bit spiky. Tansy pushed them off with a stick.
The raft went bump. It went spin. It went round and round.
Moss shut his eyes. He did not roll into a ball. Not yet.
Then a fish jumped out of the water. SPLASH!
Moss rolled into a ball.

media.alt: Moss and Pebble spin on the raft as a fish jumps out of the water

text: The ball rolled off the raft. It rolled onto a rock. It rolled up the bank on the far side.
Moss peeked out of his ball. He was wet and dizzy. But he was across!
Pebble and the raft were still spinning. Then a long stick poked out of the reeds. It gave the raft a push. The raft bumped onto the bank.
Moss saw a flash of red fur and a white tail tip. Then it was gone.
Tansy just jumped. Of course.

media.alt: Moss lands on the far bank as a stick from the reeds pushes Pebble's raft to shore

text: Next on the map was the frog rock. They walked and walked. The grass was tall. The hill was steep.
“Is it that rock?” asked Tansy. “Or that one? Or THAT one?” She ran to all of them.
“That one looks like a frog,” said Moss. And it did. It had two bumps for eyes and a long, flat grin.

media.alt: Tansy runs from rock to rock while Moss points at the frog rock

text: “Ribbit,” said Tansy to the rock. The rock did not say ribbit back.
“Next is the log with a hole,” said Pebble. She looked at the map. Then she turned it this way and that way.
“Hmm,” said Pebble. “Maybe Pip was…” She stopped. “No. Never mind.”

media.alt: Tansy talks to the frog rock while Pebble turns the map

text: The log was big and old. The hole in it was dark. Very, very dark.
“Step one: we go in!” said Tansy. She did not go in.
“Step two,” said Tansy. “Moss goes in first.”
Moss did not want to go in first. So he looked at small things.
In the mud by the log, there were fresh paw prints. Fox prints. And at the far end, there was a spot of sun.

media.alt: The three friends stop at a big, dark, hollow log, with fox prints in the mud

text: “It is not a cave,” said Moss. “It is a tunnel. The sun is on the other side.”
He went in. One small step. Then one more. Tansy and Pebble held on to his tail.
Under the log, they could hear the stream. Splish, splash.
“Do hedgehogs have tails?” asked Pebble.
“A small one,” said Moss. “Please do not pull it.”

media.alt: Moss leads the way into the log with Tansy and Pebble holding on

text: They came out in the sun. And there, in front of them, was…
Their own Hollow!
There was the stream. There was the stump. There was the gate. There was Tansy’s tree, with a big bump on it.
The log went over the stream like a bridge. They had walked in a big loop. And someone had pushed that log into place.

media.alt: The friends come out of the log and see their own Hollow and Tansy's tree

text: “We are home!” said Tansy. “That is the worst adventure ever!”
Pebble looked at the map. Then she turned it upside down. Then she groaned.
“Oh no,” she said. “Pip was… Pip was…” She shut her eyes. “I can’t say it.”
Moss took the map. He held it the other way up. Now the X was not at the top. It was at the start of the path.

media.alt: Pebble holds the map upside down and groans

text: “The X is not far away,” said Moss. “The X is here.” He tapped Tansy’s tree.
Tansy ran up the tree. She dug in a hole. Out came one acorn. Then two. Then ten. Then a whole flood of acorns!
BONK! One hit Pebble. BONK! One hit Moss.
Moss rolled into a ball. The acorns got stuck on his spines.

media.alt: Acorns pour out of Tansy's tree and bonk Pebble and Moss

text: “Moss!” said Tansy. “You look like a treasure chest!”
Moss peeked out. He was a ball of acorns. Pebble began to laugh. Tansy began to laugh.
Then Moss did too. He laughed so hard that ten acorns fell off.
Tansy put them back on. “Treasure should stay safe,” she said.

media.alt: Moss is a ball covered in acorns and everyone laughs

text: At dusk, the three friends sat under Tansy’s tree. They had a big snack of acorns.
Pip came by. “So,” he said. “Was the map upside down?”
Pebble looked at the sky. “It was a GREAT adventure,” she said. “That is all I will say.”
Up on the gate, Echo was licking his paw. “Lucky that log was there,” he said. “And lucky that raft got to shore.”
Moss looked at Echo’s muddy paws. Echo did not look at Moss.

media.alt: At dusk the friends share acorns under Tansy's tree while Pip comes by and Echo sits on the gate

text: The next day, Tansy dug a new hole for her acorns. Then she made a new map.
This time, she drew a big arrow on it. Next to the arrow, she put the word UP.
Moss smiled. He had gone over a stream and into the dark. He had been brave, one small step at a time.
And he had only rolled up… three times.

media.alt: Tansy draws a new map with an arrow while Moss smiles
